set.content: Self-Refine loops a single model through generate, critique, revise: it drafts, then is prompted separately to give specific actionable feedback on that draft, then rewrites using that feedback. Separating the critique turn from the revision turn is what makes it work — a combined 'improve this' instruction tends to produce cosmetic edits. Madaan et al. reported gains across tasks including code optimization, dialogue response and sentiment rewriting, with no additional training. A useful implementation variant, offered as practitioner guidance rather than a finding of this paper, is to constrain the critique against an explicit written list of principles rather than leaving it open-ended: the model checks the draft against each stated rule, then revises. This makes the pass auditable and repeatable, and it is the practical way to enforce style, policy or safety conventions at inference time. The important limitation is that prompted self-correction is unreliable without a dependable signal. A critical TACL survey found no convincing evidence that models reliably correct their own reasoning errors from self-generated feedback alone; self-correction works best where feedback is externally grounded — tests, validators, retrieved sources — or where the task is easy to verify but hard to produce.
set.limitations: Prompted self-correction is unreliable without external grounding; a TACL survey found no convincing evidence of reliable intrinsic reasoning self-correction. Costs at least two extra calls.

set.content: CAPO makes the cost of optimization a first-class objective rather than an afterthought. Built on evolutionary search with an LLM as the mutation operator, it adds racing — abandoning clearly losing candidates early instead of evaluating every candidate on the full set — and treats prompt length as a penalty, so shorter prompts are preferred where accuracy is comparable. Instructions and few-shot examples are optimized together. Zehle et al. evaluated fifteen combinations: five datasets (SST-5, AG News, Subj, GSM8K, COPA) across three open-weight models (Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-32B, Mistral-Small-24B), against EvoPromptGA, OPRO and PromptWizard. CAPO won in eleven of the fifteen, with the largest margin around 21 points on Llama-3.3-70B/GSM8K — but gains were small on SST-5 and AG News, so 21 points is the ceiling, not the typical case. Note the acronym: this record is the cost-aware CAPO from AutoML 2025; other, unrelated methods share the name.
